scope: October 23 daily update to edition 004: three post-review video/3D papers, two voice ecosystem updates and a Wan-Alpha++ availability correction. Older retained research and original upload dates stay explicit. Author/vendor evidence is separate from independent measurements; no local model reproduction. Excludes robotics and physical AI.

papers.title: StreamEval: pretty video can still miss the live instruction
papers.full_title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
papers.change: New v1 submitted after the October 20 12:55 UTC review. New benchmark for evolving instructions and preservation during streaming video, beyond scoring completed clips.
papers.summary: New benchmark for evolving instructions and preservation during streaming video, beyond scoring completed clips.
papers.evaluation: Authors report 37 models / 47 configurations on 300 scripted cases across five tasks, lasting 15–300 seconds, with three repeats. Vidu S2 Editing leads the three reported reference editors at 15.00/100 Edit Success, versus 8.89 for JoyAI-Video-Edit and 1.11 for XMax X2.0.
papers.caveat: Editing tables exclude configurations with Overall below 5, selected after evaluation. Automated judging and scripted scenarios limit generalization. Tasks have distinct metrics and cannot be merged into one universal ranking. Avatar customization bonuses also affect Overall.
papers.access: Public Python harness and benchmark definitions verified on GitHub; HF full split lists 300 rows. Code Apache-2.0; generated benchmark data CC BY 4.0, with separate licenses for source footage and wrapped models. Live leaderboard rendered no readable content. Commit-history endpoints failed, so exact first code/data availability is unverified.
papers.creator_implication: Editorial inference: test an edit switch and restoration while the source keeps moving; attractive footage alone cannot establish reliable live direction.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed: A small animated scene with requested-state, observed-state and preservation lanes, highlighting missed, delayed and reverted changes. Controls: Move instruction arrivals along a timeline, Choose target object and requested appearance, Adjust response lag and retention failure, Toggle visual quality versus edit success. Analytic state-machine teaching demo, not a StreamEval run or model output.
papers.review_depth: Primary submission history, methods, evaluation and caveats reviewed; project/repository availability checked; no model execution or reproduction.

papers.title: KoalaGS: which splats should survive a smaller budget?
papers.full_title: KoalaGS: Complexity-Aware Continuous Level of Detail for Gaussian Splatting
papers.change: New v1 submitted after the October 20 12:55 UTC review. Complexity-aware allocation and importance ordering keep a single trained Gaussian scene useful when only a prefix of its primitives is rendered.
papers.summary: Complexity-aware allocation and importance ordering keep a single trained Gaussian scene useful when only a prefix of its primitives is rendered.
papers.evaluation: Authors compare five baselines on 7 MipNeRF360, 2 Tanks and Temples and 2 Deep Blending scenes. On Bonsai, simulated 50-Mbps transfer of raw 236-byte primitives reaches 28 dB after 2.95 seconds, versus 3.93 for Matryoshka-GS and 14.73 for opacity-ranked MCMC.
papers.caveat: That transfer result is one simulated scene, not measured network speed. Rankings are viewpoint-independent and do not guarantee antialiasing. Image complexity misses semantic salience and view-dependent highlights. Baselines are adapted: Matryoshka training/budgets change; LightGaussian excludes recovery fine-tuning. Full-capacity or every-budget superiority is not established.
papers.access: Official project and GitHub README both say code coming soon; repository contains only README. No released implementation or weights verified.
papers.creator_implication: Editorial inference: useful for progressively loading captured scenes and showing predictable quality under a mobile rendering budget; this is neural rendering, not generative 3D.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed: Render a synthetic scene containing broad flat regions and fine details, compare which colored ellipses survive truncation, and plot error against budget. Controls: Gaussian budget from 0.1% to 100%, Opacity-only versus complexity-aware ranking, Complexity heatmap, Bandwidth and current transfer time. Analytic ranking demonstration; not trained KoalaGS, not its measured quality curve.
papers.review_depth: Primary submission history, methods, evaluation and caveats reviewed; project/repository availability checked; no model execution or reproduction.

papers.title: SplatFlux: decode a video latent into a scene you can revisit
papers.full_title: SplatFlux: Feed-Forward 4D Gaussian Reconstruction and Generation from Video Latents
papers.change: New v1 submitted after the October 20 12:55 UTC review. A shared decoder converts observed or generated video latents into 4D Gaussians, separating static structure from moving primitives. Motion interpolation supports changing time and viewpoint without rerunning a network at each timestamp.
papers.summary: A shared decoder converts observed or generated video latents into 4D Gaussians, separating static structure from moving primitives. Motion interpolation supports changing time and viewpoint without rerunning a network at each timestamp.
papers.evaluation: Author evaluations include NVIDIA Dynamic Scene, DyCheck and DAVIS reconstruction, plus SceneBench, PenguinVideoBenchmark and VBench-I2V generation. On VBench-I2V, imaging score is 72.07 versus Aether 69.85, but subject consistency is lower: 95.95 versus 97.97.
papers.caveat: Offline reconstruction/generation only. Mixed backbone comparisons and video proxy metrics do not establish universal 4D superiority. Generation adapts Wan2.1-14B; it is not a model trained independently from scratch. The paper reports roughly ten days on 32 H20 GPUs for the full training pipeline.
papers.access: Primary paper and project demos verified. The project exposes a paper link; no official runnable code, weights or their licenses were verified. Do not label open weights or a product launch.
papers.creator_implication: Editorial inference: promising for re-framing moving content after generation; generation, reconstruction, and novel-view rendering must remain distinct in explanations.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed: A colored Gaussian scene with fixed background splats and moving foreground splats; separate panels reveal static aggregation and dynamic interpolation. Controls: Independent time and camera-orbit sliders, Static/dynamic probability threshold, Velocity-arrow display, Interpolation amount and occlusion overlay. Synthetic analytic Gaussian demonstration, not SplatFlux inference or recovered geometry.
papers.review_depth: Primary submission history, methods, evaluation and caveats reviewed; project/repository availability checked; no model execution or reproduction.

papers.title: Phonon: local speech that arrives before the whole sentence finishes.
papers.full_title: Gradium Phonon open-weight models and first stable runtime 0.4.0
papers.change: First stable Rust runtime released October 20 at 13:36:55 UTC, after the previous 12:55:59 review. Official announcement is October 20; initial model uploads are October 19. These are distinct dates.
papers.summary: Flow matching predicts audio latents in 80 ms frames, decoded by Mimi. Runtime supports incremental audio on desktop, phone and browser. Advertised 31M/40M counts exclude the audio tokenizer.
papers.evaluation: Vendor-run English listening comparison: 468 raters and 8,290 votes; 31M Elo 2098 versus Kokoro 2043 in this selected pool. LLM-assisted WER covers hard structured sentences and Seed-TTS text. No independent reproduction here.
papers.caveat: Long-text splitting loses cross-sentence prosody; text normalization needs the correct language. Runtime speed and quality claims are setup-specific. Do not infer whole-system size from language-model parameter count.
papers.access: Runtime and 31M English model available; 31M Apache 2.0 and ungated. 40M language-specific and multilingual weights are gated and CC BY-NC 4.0. No model downloaded or executed; no access terms accepted.
papers.creator_implication: A candidate for local scratch narration and interactive audio previews. Commercial permissions differ between the 31M and 40M models.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed: drag a playhead over 80 ms latent frames, decoder chunks and playback buffers; vary generation rate and startup buffer to explain first audio versus sustained real time. Extend the Ming latency concept with actual incremental generation. Analytic teaching model, not Phonon inference.
papers.review_depth: Official announcement, release timestamp, model cards and unauthenticated Hub metadata; no local inference.

papers.title: KittenTTS 2: one exempt token can turn narration into silence.
papers.full_title: KittenTTS 2 silence-token repetition fix and 0.9.6 update
papers.change: October 21 fixes silence-token repetition handling and bumps 0.9.6; October 22 adds a Gradio demo. KittenTTS 2 code was integrated October 2 and its Hub repo existed September 30. The October 22 Reddit headline is not its original release date.
papers.summary: The sampling correction stops exempting silence codec 4299 from repetition penalties. Speech-end and STOP stay exempt. Maintainers say this addresses silent tails, dropped sentences and runs to the token cap; shared vLLM processing and MLX were updated.
papers.evaluation: Code diff and timestamps verified. No measured local fix validation or independent SOTA comparison. Reddit listening reports are mixed anecdotes. Model expression controls remain beta.
papers.caveat: Ternary linear layers do not make the entire pipeline 1.58-bit; embeddings, scales and decoder differ. Chunk-level streaming waits for each completed chunk. Exact voice totals differ across docs, so no catalog count is promoted.
papers.access: Apache 2.0 package; weights separately use Stellon Labs Community License, with limited commercial grant and a USD 1 million revenue/funding threshold. Official files are available; no inference run.
papers.creator_implication: Existing users should check the fix when narration stalls or drops lines. Do not treat the Reddit open-source/SOTA label as proof of unrestricted commercial use or superior voice quality.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed: categorical probability bars for speech, silence and end tokens, with a repetition-window slider and exemption switches. Show how exempting silence can trap sampling, while penalizing end tokens can prevent termination. Analytic toy, not measured KittenTTS output.
papers.review_depth: Primary fix diff, code history, Hub metadata/model card/license and indexed discussion; no independent listening test.

papers.title: Wan-Alpha++: animate the asset, including its disappearance.
papers.full_title: Wan-Alpha++: Animating a Single RGBA Asset into Controllable Transparent Video Effects
papers.date: 19 Oct paper/weight upload · 20 Oct code · corrected 23 Oct
papers.change: Correction to October 20 coverage: ordinary RGBA I2V adapters and inference code are public in a separate repository. Weight files were uploaded October 19 at 11:44 UTC; initial code commit is October 20 at 09:34 UTC, both before the previous review. This is a missed availability distinction, not a new October 23 release.
papers.summary: Temporal phase reparameterization moves visible content to conditioning boundaries, then restores the transparent-visible-transparent effect. Uses Wan2.1-I2V-14B with shared RGBA latents and transparent-state guidance.
papers.evaluation: Authors evaluate 60 image-conditioned videos, with 81 frames at 480×832 and 40 sampling steps. Effect-reference DINO-I rises 0.6679→0.9227 against Wan2.1-FLF2V plus MatAnyone. Appearance metrics include only sufficiently visible frames. Forty participants rank effects.
papers.caveat: The released ordinary RGBA Wan2.2 path differs from the paper’s Wan2.1 effect evaluation. Its checked-in example uses eight processes; no low-memory support or output quality verified. The 196-clip effect study and four-step earlier T2V results cannot be transferred to this release.
papers.access: Ordinary RGBA inference uses Wan2.2-I2V-A14B with high/low-noise adapters and the separate Wan-Alpha VAE. Both adapter files verified in the October 19 HF commit tree; model-card metadata says Apache-2.0. Effect-specific RGBA checkpoints and training code remain pending. No inference or weight download; standalone code license not verified.
papers.creator_implication: Potentially useful for compositable smoke, glow or magical effects with an explicit reference asset.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed analytic alpha timeline: scrub an effect fading in/out, drag the visible reference frame and phase offset, and switch checkerboard or colored backgrounds. Show original versus shifted timelines and reconstruct the final composite. Teach why an empty first frame carries little appearance information.
papers.review_depth: Primary repository, model card, public GitHub/HF commit APIs and historical file tree. October 20 conclusion corrected; paper metrics retained as the paper’s separate effect evaluation.

papers.title: FluidGen: teach the smoke model what moves, not just what it looks like.
papers.full_title: FluidGen: Physics-Aware Fluid Video Generation via Motion-Guided Post-Training
papers.change: New generative VFX research for smoke, fire and explosions; fits filmmaking rather than robotics. Submitted October 19; newly discovered in the October 20 arXiv listing after the previous review, not an October 20 launch.
papers.summary: A Wan2.1-I2V-14B extension jointly predicts RGB and pixel-aligned 3D velocity. Simulation-supervised motion supports velocity-based DPO rewards.
papers.evaluation: Author tests: 15 FluidNexus sequences and 20 in-the-wild images. Final FVD 199.2 versus base Wan 569.7; supervised-only 192.1. DPO improves VBench imaging quality 0.4282→0.4627 while PSNR and subject consistency decline slightly.
papers.caveat: Small selected evaluation; no independent reproduction or broad current-model ranking. Reward scores physical plausibility rather than enforcing Navier–Stokes. Predicted physical velocity and the latent flow-matching velocity are different quantities. Artist control of predicted velocity is future work.
papers.access: Official project explicitly marks code and data as coming soon; no weights or runnable release verified.
papers.creator_implication: Research direction for coherent fluid VFX; project shows keyframe-guided smoke transformations and Houdini transfer demonstrations, not independently tested production reliability.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed analytic smoke lab: advect colored density through a 2D velocity field; expose curl, divergence, viscosity and timestep, plus arrow/color encodings. Contrast physical scene motion with a separate latent flow trajectory. Add a reward-versus-fidelity panel to explain DPO tradeoffs. Label as a numerical teaching simulation, not FluidGen inference.
papers.review_depth: Primary method/evaluation/ablations/conclusion/history and official project status verified.

papers.title: ResStreamGS: stop sending the whole scene every frame.
papers.full_title: ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming
papers.summary: Caches stable splats per frame group; updates attribute-sensitive splats frame by frame.
papers.change: October 15 v1, covered in the October 16 delta and carried into this weekly synthesis with a new original interactive. Not a new October 19 release.
papers.evaluation: Author tests: six 300-frame sequences, held-out cameras, 20-frame groups. Against a controlled V3-style baseline: +7.51–8.35 dB PSNR and 21.4–56.5% lower amortized payload. 30.883 FPS on one Snapdragon 778G phone.
papers.caveat: Payload is not wireless performance. Culling and pruning also improve speed. Abrupt changes challenge fixed groups; GIFStream has smaller payloads.
papers.access: Full paper reviewed; implementation not verified, no reproduction.
papers.creator_implication: For captured volumetric scenes. Stationary splats can still need appearance updates.
papers.review_depth: Primary methods, evaluation, ablations and submission history.
